story: On a sunny Friday afternoon in Sumter Oaks, Gary tells Hal he'll get the golf cart paperwork filed before any bulbs go on, then heads off to play a game with Donna, who is already walking toward the Rec Center. Hal stays on Magnolia Loop, dutifully counting the flamingos in Donna's flock and writing the tally in his log. Meanwhile, Rosa, eager as ever, is at home in her kitchen tasting her main dish for seasoning, covering the sides, and noting what's still missing.
events: Hal (donna flamingo flock): Count the flamingos visible from the street and write the number in my log
Rosa (rosa kitchen): Taste the main dish for seasoning, cover the sides, and jot down anything still missing

gary.thought_process: Hal just reminded me that L-01 requires the cart lights to be filed with the Architectural Review committee before I mount anything, and I'm not sure my request was ever actually filed. Donna's been waiting on me for the courts since noon, and I already apologized and promised lemonades, so the right move is to stop chatting and get going. I'll tell Hal I'll get the paperwork sorted, then head to the rec center with Donna. I'll finish the wiring and the filing afterward.

parameters.content: Understood, Hal. I'll get it filed properly before a single bulb goes on that cart. Right now I owe Donna a game, so I'll catch you after.

donna.thought_process: Gary just said he's ready with paddle in hand, and it's 2:17 on a Friday. The courts are open and I've been chasing the ladder all week. Hal has the flamingo count on his log, but the last thing I did was start pulling the extras from the yard, and he's offered to drop it if we're at three. I shouldn't repeat my invitation too much or dawdle with Hal. The best move is to get Gary moving toward the rec center right now, so I'll head over with him and let the flamingos situation stay settled. Actually, I'm the one who needs to lead the way, so I'll say it short and go.

parameters.content: Heading to the rec center courts with Gary to get our practice game in and keep our spot on the ladder.

hal.thought_process: Donna's flock is right here on the loop, and the order to pull the extras was already given this morning. Gary is off to pickleball and I've told him all I need to about L-01. I won't nag Donna again, since I've already told her to get it down to three. The honest move is to check the flock myself, count what's visible from the street, and put the number in my log. Facts for the committee, not a fight.

parameters.content: Count the flamingos visible from the street and write the number in my log

rosa.thought_process: It's 2:17 PM and dinner is tonight. I've stirred the main dish, tasted it, set the places, and checked my shift schedule already, so the big pieces are done. The sides should be staged and covered, and I last noted I still needed a final check and a list of anything missing. Another pass at the kitchen to taste for seasoning, jot down any gaps, and cover the sides to keep them warm is the most useful thing. No one is nearby, so no one to talk to. Nothing left to second-guess about the schedule.

parameters.content: Taste the main dish for seasoning, cover the sides, and jot down anything still missing

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
